We need to determine SMILES for compound with formula C10H14, DBE=4, 10 unique carbon environments, 5 unique hydrogen environments, 0 aromatic carbons, 3 methyl groups, 0 carbonyls. Also fragments list given seems irrelevant (they are anionic fragments). Likely a non-aromatic hydrocarbon with 3 methyl groups, 10 carbons, 14 hydrogens => degree of unsaturation 4. No aromatic, so unsaturation likely from double bonds and/or rings. DBE 4 could be 4 double bonds, or 2 double + 2 rings, etc. 10 unique carbon environments suggests each carbon is chemically distinct (no symmetry). 5 unique hydrogen environments. 3 methyl groups distinct.

Actually methyl carbon is extra carbon attached to ring carbon, not part of ring. So adding three methyl groups adds 3 carbons beyond the 6 ring + side chain 4 =13 >10. So not possible.

Thus methyl groups must be part of the 10 carbons, not extra beyond ring+side chain. So maybe the backbone is not a ring but linear.
